note: Sanitized. Fictional provider values only. No account credential or secret is recorded.

steps.action: Open Settings > Organization > Integrations > E-signature; check the unconfigured card
steps.actual: /settings/integrations forwards to /settings/integrations/e-signature. The Settings rail has an Integrations entry for this address. The DocuSign card starts collapsed with the Not connected chip.

steps.action: Expand DocuSign; check default controls in Polling mode
steps.actual: Environment Demo and Signing updates Polling by default. Polling hint: "Keeps OpenLaw private. Only outbound access to DocuSign is needed. Updates can take about 15 to 20 minutes while the worker is running. Documents are still sent to DocuSign for signing.". Integration key, User ID and RSA private key are shown. Public callback URL, Connect HMAC secret and Webhook URL are absent. Test connection is disabled. No switch and no Remove connector.

steps.action: Select Save connector with every field blank (Polling)
steps.actual: The browser refused the submit. No request reached the API. Required fields reported missing: ds-integration-key, ds-user-id, ds-private-key.

steps.action: Choose Webhook; check the extra fields and the missing-HMAC refusal
steps.actual: Webhook shows Public callback URL and Connect HMAC secret with the hint "Required. OpenLaw checks it on every delivery...". Webhook hint: "Receives updates as DocuSign delivers them. Requires a public HTTPS gateway and a signed Connect subscription. OpenLaw also checks periodically to recover missed updates.". With the HMAC secret blank the browser refused the submit and no request was sent.

steps.action: Webhook: enter a non-HTTPS Public callback URL and save
steps.actual: The browser accepted the http:// address. The API refused the save and no connector was created. The pane showed only the generic "One or more request fields are invalid.". It did not show the API's rule ("Use an HTTPS callback URL without credentials, query parameters or fragments."), so the reader cannot learn the rule from the pane.

steps.action: API refusals for incomplete saves (authenticated requests, no browser navigation)
steps.actual: Polling without an RSA key: 400 "Paste the RSA private key DocuSign issued for the integration.". Webhook without a Connect secret: 400 "Paste the DocuSign Connect HMAC secret before selecting Webhook.". Blank Integration key and User ID: 400 (validation). No connector was created.

steps.action: Save a fictional connector in Polling mode; reload; check the saved state
steps.actual: The chip reads Connected and Send for signature from records is on. After reload the RSA private key input is blank with the keep/rotate hint. Test connection is enabled. No Webhook URL row in Polling mode.

steps.action: Test connection with the unreadable fictional key
steps.actual: The pane showed "The connection test failed. The stored RSA private key could not be read. Paste the key DocuSign issued, including its BEGIN and END lines." The Connected chip still showed, which matches the article: the chip does not prove the credentials work.

steps.action: Change the saved Polling connector to Webhook without an HMAC secret, then with one
steps.actual: Without the Connect HMAC secret the browser blocked the save. With a fictional secret the save succeeded without re-entering the RSA key, and the Webhook URL row appeared: http://127.0.0.1:23314/api/v1/signing/docusign/webhook.

steps.action: Webhook mode: post an unsigned and a signed fictional delivery for an unknown Envelope
steps.actual: Unsigned delivery: HTTP 401. Delivery signed with the saved fictional secret, naming an unknown Envelope: HTTP 204 (acknowledged, nothing changed).

steps.action: Switch back to Polling; check the Webhook fields leave and a signed delivery is refused
steps.actual: Polling hides the callback and HMAC fields and removes the Webhook URL row after save. The stored Connect secret remains (hasWebhookSecret true), yet a correctly signed delivery now gets HTTP 401.

steps.action: Turn off Send for signature from records; test; save a change while off
steps.actual: Chip reads Turned off; hint "Off since Sep 16. Records show the manual path, and rounds already out stand still until you turn this back on.". Test connection stays enabled; selecting it shows "No e-signature connector is configured. Save the credentials first." Saving a changed User ID while off stored the change and left the connector off. A delivery while off: HTTP 401.

steps.action: Turn the connector back on, then remove it
steps.actual: Turning on restored Connected. The remove dialog says: "Remove the DocuSign connector The RSA key and the Connect secret are deleted with the connector. Reconnecting means pasting both again. Records go back to the manual path. To stop sending and keep the credentials, turn the connector off instead. Cancel Remove connector". After confirming, the chip reads Not connected, the form is blank and Signing updates is back to Polling. The API reports configured false.

steps.action: Open Settings > Organization > AI analysis; check the unconfigured page
steps.actual: AI analysis is its own Organization rail entry. Provider starts collapsed with Not connected. Field prompts is open, has no collapse control and holds 7 prompts, with a Contracts → Fields link to /settings/contracts/fields. No Request conversion card is shown before a connector is saved.

steps.action: Expand Provider; check presets and the default Anthropic form
steps.actual: Presets: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, Custom endpoint. Default preset Anthropic with prefilled model claude-sonnet-5. The API key hint says it is required. Load models is disabled until a key is typed. Test connection is disabled.

steps.action: Select Save connector with no API key
steps.actual: The browser refused the submit because API key is required. No request reached the API.

steps.action: Check the OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI, Ollama and Custom endpoint forms
steps.actual: OpenRouter: model "~openai/gpt-latest", Base URL shown=false, Load models shown=true. Azure OpenAI: Deployment endpoint=true, manual model input=true, Load models buttons=0. Ollama: key optional hint=true, Base URL shown=false. Custom endpoint: Protocol options=Anthropic Messages / OpenAI-compatible chat completions / Gemini, Base URL shown=true, model ""

steps.action: Custom endpoint: save a Base URL that contains credentials
steps.actual: The pane showed "The provider base URL must not contain credentials." No connector was created.

steps.action: API refusals for incomplete or invalid AI saves (authenticated requests)
steps.actual: OpenRouter without key: 400 "Paste the API key for this provider.". Custom with ftp URL: 400 "The provider base URL must use HTTP or HTTPS.". Custom without Protocol: 400 "Choose the protocol used by the custom endpoint.". Blank model: 400. Azure Load models: 400 "Enter the deployment name from Azure manually. This endpoint does not list deployments.". Test with no connector: 400 "No enabled AI connector is configured. Save it first."

steps.action: Load models against a closed loopback endpoint
steps.actual: Load models showed "The provider model list could not be reached or read." beside the control. Nothing was saved.

steps.action: Save the fictional Custom endpoint; check chip, switch, Request conversion card; test
steps.actual: Chip reads Connected; Use AI analysis switch shown. Request conversion card appeared (matter-preparation: checked=false, enabled=true; contract-preparation: checked=false, enabled=true; contract-conversion-analysis: checked=false, enabled=true). Card order: Personal > Organization > Provider > Request conversion > Field prompts. Test connection showed "The connection test failed. The provider could not be reached. bad port"

steps.action: Reload; check key retention hint and key requirement after changing the endpoint
steps.actual: After reload the API key input is blank with the keep/rotate hint. Changing Base URL switches the hint to required, and the browser blocks a save without a new key.

steps.action: Turn off Use AI analysis; check Test and Request conversion; save while off
steps.actual: Chip reads Turned off; hint "Off since Sep 16. Turn it on to make AI analysis available again.". Test connection and the three Request conversion switches are disabled. Saving a changed Model stored it and left the connector off. The test API answers 400 "No enabled AI connector is configured. Save it first.".

steps.action: Type in a core Field prompt, press Escape, reload
steps.actual: Check did not complete: On ai-field-prompt-term_type: the box showed the saved text right after Escape (true). Save requests sent after Escape: 1. After reload the abandoned text was stored. The article says Escape restores the saved text. The fixture prompt was reset to its default through the API afterwards.

steps.action: Save a core Field prompt with Enter, clear it, then Reset to default
steps.actual: On ai-field-prompt-term_type: Enter saved the edit and showed Reset to default. Clearing the box and leaving it restored the saved text (no blank save). Reset to default restored the built-in prompt and removed the link. maxlength is 2000.

steps.action: Remove the AI connector
steps.actual: Dialog says "Remove the AI connector The API key is deleted with the connector. Reconnecting means entering it again. Cancel Remove connector". After confirming, the chip reads Not connected, the Request conversion card is gone, and the form is back to Anthropic.

steps.action: Open both Settings pages as a Legal Team Member
steps.actual: Both addresses forward to /settings/profile. The Organization rail group is absent. The connector APIs answer 403 and 403.
